preamble: Latin /b/ followed by yod became /ʒ/ in French through a multi-stage path: the labial was palatalized and replaced by an affricate [dʒ], which later deaffricated to [ʒ] (Late Latin rabia > Old French rage [radʒə] > Modern French rage [ʁaʒ]). The change is conditioned by the following /j/ and is essentially restricted to Gallo-Romance; no comparable regular b > ʒ shift is well documented outside it.

examples.note: The -bj- cluster passed through Old French [dʒ] before deaffricating to [ʒ].
Old French gojon/goujon; the -bi- before a vowel was treated as -bj-.

sources: Alkire, T., & Rosen, C. (2010). Romance Languages: A Historical Introduction. Cambridge University Press.
